2026-12-02-sim-p4.notes: Work: psl-antoine-lmtd = process-sim-lab PR #8 (MERGED 2026-11-17, merge 01c6c10). I read it with gh pr view and gh pr diff. The diff confirms: Antoine log10(P/bar) = A - B/(T+C); NIST constants for benzene, toluene and ethylbenzene; ValueError outside t_min..t_max; test_normal_boiling_points_match_nist_within_its_uncertainty, whose tolerance is the stated NIST uncertainty; and the PR text 'Water is left out on purpose'. I ran water_antoine.py and its output matches .expected. I fetched the NIST water page: all 7 Antoine rows match, including Bridgeman and Aldrich 344-373 (5.08354/1663.125/-45.622) and Stull 255.9-373 (4.6543/1435.264/-64.848). The IF97 Table 34 coefficients are right, Table 35 is reproduced, and Tsat(101325 Pa) = 373.124 K. As an independent check against Wagner-Pruss (IAPWS-95 auxiliary saturation equation), Stull gives -0.266 / +0.387 / +0.473 K at 330/370/373 K and B&A +0.024..+0.031 K, so the numbers hold. Problems: (1) Imprecise. LinkedIn calls IAPWS-IF97 'the reference equation for water', and Facebook says 'the international reference equation'. IF97 is the Industrial Formulation. The IAPWS page itself says it is 'recommended for industrial use'. The scientific reference is IAPWS-95, and IF97 is fitted to it. Numbers do not change, but a thermo reader will flag it. Fix: say 'the IAPWS-IF97 industrial formulation', or compare with IAPWS-95/Wagner-Pruss. (2) The headline number is framed as 'still inside the fit's valid range', but 373 K is exactly the fit's upper end point (t_max = 373.0). The honest interior value is 0.39 K at 370 K. Fix: say 'at the top end of its range', or lead with 0.39 K at 370 K. (3) Work link (why sources is 3): the merged change shows the range guard, the NIST Tb test and leaving water out, and the post describes those correctly. The water fits vs IAPWS comparison behind the hook number, the card, the Short and every channel is new analysis done for the post ('For this post I checked'). It is not in PR #8 or any ledger entry. It is honestly labelled, but the post's central measurement is not merged project work. The PR also states water's normal boiling point as 373.15 K, and the post silently uses 373.12 K. To raise: merge the water check into process-sim-lab (for example a test or note that compares the NIST water fits with IAPWS) and add it to work.yaml, or rebuild the hook around what PR #8 does. (4) One idea is clear, but LinkedIn spends two paragraphs on benzene, toluene and ethylbenzene before the water point.
